text:
It’s fascinating that AI is making us more aware of the cost of communication than we've ever been with other humans.

Every extra iteration costs something. Every "one more thing," clarification, follow-up — it all consumes resources. What if we treated conversations with people the same way?

Recently, I started an important discussion with my team. It began with a few questions that I thought would help us align. Somehow, it went in every possible direction except the one I expected.

We eventually reached an understanding. But getting there required countless messages and a lot of time.

If this had been an exchange with Claude, I would've watched every extra iteration because I know each one costs money. So why don't we think the same way when we talk to each other?

Human interactions aren't free either, right? Every unnecessary misunderstanding has a cost. But the currency just isn't dollars or tokens.

Maybe better communication doesn't start with better prompts. Maybe it starts with treating another person's resources as just as valuable as the ones we spend talking to AI.

What do you think? Would we communicate differently if every extra exchange with another person came with a visible price tag?
